sivst-p01.speaker: Utpaladeva, devotional voice (stotra)
sivst-p01.question: What is the nature of bhakti, and how does it relate to recognition (pratyabhijñā)?
premises: Stotra 1 (bhaktivilāsa): na dhyāyato na japataḥ syād yasyāvidhipūrvakam — not for one who meditates without rule, nor for one who chants without preparation. Śivabhāsas taṃ numo bhaktiśālinam — we bow to Śiva's light, the bhakti-possessor.
Ātmā mama bhavadbhaktisudhāpānayuvāpi san — my self, drinking bhakti-nectar, though young. Lokayātrārajorāgāt palitair iva dhūsaraḥ — like grey with dust of world-journey.

Labdhatatsaṃpadāṃ bhaktimatāṃ tvatpuravāsinām — of bhakti-possessors who have gained that wealth, city-dwellers. Saṃcāro lokamārge 'pi syāt tayaiva vijṛmbhayā — movement in world-path by that expansion.

Sākṣādbhavanmaye nātha sarvasmin bhuvanāntare | kiṃ na bhaktimatāṃ kṣetram mantraḥ kvaiṣām na siddhyati — Lord, in all worlds where Śiva is directly present, what is not the bhakti-possessor's field; what mantra of theirs does not succeed.
Jayanti bhaktipīyūṣarasāsavavaronmadāḥ — victorious, intoxicated with best bhakti-nectar-wine. Advitīyā api sadā tvaddvitīyā api prabho — even non-dual, always your second, Lord.
Anantānandasindhos te nātha tattvaṃ vidanti te — they know your truth, ocean of endless bliss. Tādṛśa eva ye sāndrabhaktānandarasāplutāḥ — such are those drenched in dense bhakti-bliss-nectar.

Tvam evātmeśa sarvasya sarvaś cātmani rāgavān | iti svabhāvasiddhāṃs tvadbhaktiṃ jānañ jayej janaḥ — you alone are self-Lord of all; all is in self, attached; thus knowing bhakti as self-established, one conquers people.

Nātha vedyakṣaye kena na dṛśyo 'syekakaḥ sthitaḥ | vedyavedakasaṃkṣobhe 'py asi bhaktaiḥ sudarśanaḥ — Lord, when knowable is destroyed, by whom are you not seen standing alone; in knowable-knower-agitation, you are easily seen by bhaktas.
Anantānandasarasī devī priyatamā yathā | aviyuktāsti te tadvad ekā tvadbhaktir astu me — as the lake of endless bliss, the beloved goddess, inseparable from you; so may one bhakti be mine.

Sarva eva bhavallābhahetur bhaktimatāṃ vibho — all is cause of gaining you for bhakti-possessors, Lord. Saṃvinmārgo 'yam āhlādaduḥkhamohais tridhā sthitaḥ — this consciousness-path stands threefold with joy/suffering/delusion.

Bhavadbhaktyamṛtāsvādād bodhasya syāt parāpi yā | daśā sā māṃ prati svāmin nāsavasyeva śuktatā — from tasting bhakti-nectar, even the supreme state of knowledge; that state, Lord, for me, like vinegar's sourness for wine.
Stotras 2–4: recognition in devotional mode (sarvātmaparibhāvana — contemplation of the all-soul; praṇayaprasāda — gift of affection; surasodara — potent nectar).
sivst-p01.inference: Bhakti is supreme: not for one who meditates without rule; we bow to Śiva's light, the bhakti-possessor. Bhakti-possessors move in the world by expansion; no mantra fails for them; they are intoxicated with bhakti-nectar. Even non-dual, they are always Śiva's second. They know Śiva's truth, the ocean of endless bliss. Bhakti is self-established; Śiva is easily seen by bhaktas; bhakti is inseparable from Śiva. The consciousness-path is threefold (joy/suffering/delusion); the knowledge-state is like vinegar-sourness compared to bhakti-nectar. Recognition (pratyabhijñā) in devotional mode: Śiva as all, the world as his body, the devotee's recognition that all is Śiva.
sivst-p01.conclusion: Bhakti is supreme and self-established; Śiva is easily seen by bhaktas; bhakti is inseparable from Śiva. Recognition (pratyabhijñā) operates in devotional mode: the devotee recognizes all as Śiva. The knowledge-state is like vinegar-sourness compared to bhakti-nectar.
sivst-p01.theorem: bhakti = svabhāvasiddha (self-established); Śiva is easily seen by bhaktas; bhakti is inseparable from Śiva; pratyabhijñā in devotional mode.

sivst-p02.speaker: Utpaladeva, devotional voice (stotra)
sivst-p02.question: What is svātantrya (autonomy) in devotional mode? What is āveśa (possession by the deity)?
premises: Stotra 5 (svabalanideśana): tvatpādapadmasamparkamātrasambhogasaṅginam — one who enjoys only the contact of your lotus-feet. Galepādikayā nātha māṃ svaveśma praveśaya — Lord, bring me into your abode. Bhavatpādāmbujarajorājirañjitamūrdhajaḥ — my hair adorned with the dust of your lotus-feet. Apārarabhasārabdhanartanaḥ syām ahaṃ kadā — when shall I dance with unrestrained speed? Tvad ekanātho bhagavann iyad evārthaye sadā — Lord, I always beg only this: that you be my sole master. Tvadantarvasatir mūko bhaveyaṃ mānyathā budhaḥ — dwelling within you, may I be silent; otherwise I am wise (and that is the problem).

Stotra 6 (adhvavisphuraṇa): kṣaṇamātram apīśāna viyuktasya tvayā mama — even for a moment, Lord, separated from you. Nibiḍaṃ tapyamānasya sadā bhūyā dṛśaḥ padam — may I always have the state of seeing, being intensely scorched. Viyogasāre saṃsāre priyeṇa prabhuṇā tvayā | aviyuktaḥ sadaiva syāṃ jagatāpi viyojitaḥ — in the essence of separation (saṃsāra), by you, the dear Lord, may I always be unseparated, even separated from the world. Kāyavāṅmanasair yatra yāmi sarvaṃ tvam eva tat — wherever I go with body, speech, mind — all that is you.

Stotra 7 (vidhuravijaya): tvatpādapadmasamparkamātrasambhogasaṅginam — one who enjoys only the contact of your lotus-feet. Galepādikayā nātha māṃ svaveśma praveśaya — Lord, bring me into your abode. Bhavatpādāmbujarajorājirañjitamūrdhajaḥ — my hair adorned with the dust of your lotus-feet. Apārarabhasārabdhanartanaḥ syām ahaṃ kadā — when shall I dance with unrestrained speed? Tvad ekanātho bhagavann iyad evārthaye sadā — Lord, I always beg only this: that you be my sole master. Tvadantarvasatir mūko bhaveyaṃ mānyathā budhaḥ — dwelling within you, may I be silent; otherwise I am wise.

Stotra 8 (alaukikodbala): tvatpādapadmasamparkamātrasambhogasaṅginam — one who enjoys only the contact of your lotus-feet. Viyogasāre saṃsāre priyeṇa prabhuṇā tvayā | aviyuktaḥ sadaiva syāṃ jagatāpi viyojitaḥ — in the essence of separation (saṃsāra), by you, the dear Lord, may I always be unseparated, even separated from the world. Kāyavāṅmanasair yatra yāmi sarvaṃ tvam eva tat — wherever I go with body, speech, mind — all that is you. Bhavadaṅgapariṣvaṅgasambhogaḥ svecchayaiva me | ghaṭatām — may the enjoyment of embracing your body happen by your will. Prakaṭībhava nānyābhiḥ prārthanābhiḥ kadarthanāḥ — reveal yourself; let not other prayers torment.
sivst-p02.inference: Stotras 5–8 shift from bhakti-as-supreme to svātantrya (autonomy/freedom) in devotional mode. The devotee's stance: 'I am yours, do with me what you will.' Āveśa (possession by the deity) is the key experience: the devotee is so filled with Śiva that the distinction between worshipper and worshipped dissolves. The devotional voice cajoles, longs, and surrenders. This is the 'soul of the practices' (Gitananda): the feeling and emotional intensity with which the upāyas are done. The key move: tvadantarvasatir mūko bhaveyaṃ — dwelling within you, may I be silent; otherwise I am wise (and that is the problem). The devotee's wisdom is an obstacle; silence (āveśa) is the goal.
sivst-p02.conclusion: Svātantrya in devotional mode: the devotee surrenders autonomy to Śiva. Āveśa (possession by the deity) dissolves the worshipper/worshipped distinction. The devotional voice cajoles, longs, surrenders. Key: tvadantarvasatir mūko bhaveyaṃ (dwelling within you, may I be silent).
sivst-p02.theorem: svātantrya in devotional mode = āveśa (possession by the deity); the devotee's wisdom is an obstacle; silence (āveśa) is the goal.

sivst-p03.speaker: Utpaladeva, devotional voice (stotra)
sivst-p03.question: What is autonomy (svātantrya) in devotional mode? What is the arcane lore (rahasya)?
premises: Stotra 9 (svātantryavijaya): kadā navarasārdrārdrasambhogāsvādanotsukam | pravarteta vihāyānyan mama tvatsparśane manaḥ — when will my mind, eager to taste the nine rasas soaked in devotion, turn away from other things to touch you? Tvadekaraktas tvatpādapūjāmātramahādhanaḥ — attached to you alone, with the great wealth of worshipping your feet. Kadā sākṣātkariṣyāmi bhavantam ayam utsukaḥ — when, eager, shall I realize you directly? Gāḍhānurāgavaśato nirapekṣībhūtamānaso 'smi — by the force of deep love, my mind has become free of expectation. Kadā paṭapaṭiti vighaṭitākhilamahārgalas tvām upaiṣyāmi — when, with all great bolts broken at once, shall I approach you? Svasaṃvitsārahṛdayādhiṣṭhānāḥ sarvadevatāḥ — all deities stationed in the essence of self-awareness. Kadā nātha vaśīkuryāṃ bhavadbhaktiprabhāvataḥ — when, Lord, shall I subjugate by the power of devotion to you? Kadā me syād vibho bhūri bhaktyānandarasotsavaḥ — when, Lord, shall I have the great festival of bliss-nectar of devotion? Yadālokasukhānandī pṛthaṅ nāmāpi lapsyate — when even the name, delighting in the happiness of seeing, shall be obtained. Īśvaram abhayam udāraṃ pūrṇam akāraṇam apahnutātmānaṃ — the Lord, fearless, generous, full, causeless, self-concealed. Sahasābhijñāya kadā svāmijanaṃ lajjayiṣyāmi — when, suddenly recognizing, shall I put to shame the Lord's people? Kadā kām api tāṃ nātha tava vallabhatām iyām — when, Lord, shall I attain that beloved-ness of yours? Yayā māṃ prati na kvāpi yuktaṃ te syāt palāyitum — by which it would not be fitting for you to flee from me anywhere. Tattvato 'śeṣajantūnāṃ bhavatpūjāmayātmanām | dṛṣṭyānumoditarasāplāvitaḥ syāṃ kadā vibho — when, Lord, shall I be flooded with the nectar of approval by the vision of all beings whose self is worship of you? Jñānasya paramā bhūmir yogasya paramā daśā | tvadbhaktir yā vibho karhi pūrṇa me syāt tadarthitā — the supreme ground of knowledge, the supreme state of yoga — when, Lord, shall devotion to you be full, with the desire for that? Sahasāivasādya kadā gāḍham avaṣṭabhya harṣavivaśo 'ham — when, suddenly today, having firmly grasped, I shall be overcome with joy? Tvaccaraṇavaranidhānaṃ sarvasya prakaṭayiṣyāmi — I shall reveal the treasure of your supreme feet to all. Paritaḥ prasaracchuddhatvadālokamayaḥ kadā | syāṃ yatheśa na kiñcin me māyācchāyābilaṃ bhavet — when, Lord, shall I be, as you are, with no cave of Māyā's shadow in me? Ātmasātkṛtaniḥśeṣamaṇḍalo nirvyapekṣakaḥ — having made all the universe my own, free of dependence. Kadā bhaveyaṃ bhagavaṃs tvadbhaktagaṇanāyakaḥ — when, Lord, shall I be the leader of the troop of your bhaktas? Nātha lokābhimānānām apūrvaṃ tvaṃ nibandhanam — Lord, you are the unprecedented bond of worldly pride. Mahābhimānaḥ karhi syāṃ tvadbhaktirasapūritaḥ — when shall I be filled with great pride, filled with the nectar of devotion to you? Aśeṣaviṣayāśūnyaśrīsamāśleṣasusthitaḥ — established in the embrace of the glory free from all objects. Śayīyam iva śītāṅghrikuśeśayayuge kadā — when, like a swan on the cool lotus-feet. Bhaktyāsavasamṛddhāyās tvatpūjābhogasampadaḥ — the wealth of enjoying the worship of you, rich with the nectar of devotion. Kadā pāraṃ gamiṣyāmi bhaviṣyāmi kadā kṛtī — when shall I cross over, when shall I be accomplished? Ānandabāṣpapūraskhalitaparibhrāntagadgadākrandaḥ — stammering, stumbling, with tears of joy, crying out. Hāsollāsitavadanas tvatsparśarasaṃ kadāpsyāmi — when, with laughing face, shall I taste the nectar of touching you? Paśujanasamānavṛttām avadhūya daśām imāṃ kadā śambho — when, Śambhu, shall I shake off this state resembling the bound soul? Āsvādayeya tāvakabhaktocitam ātmano rūpam — when shall I taste the form of my self, fit for devotion to you? Labdhāṇimādisiddhir vigalitasakalopatāpasantrāsaḥ — having obtained the siddhis of aṇimā etc., free from all distress and fear. Tvadbhaktirasāyanapānakriḍhāniṣṭaḥ kadāsīya nātha — when, Lord, shall I be one who delights in drinking the elixir of devotion to you? Kadā sa tathāvidha ākrando me samuccared vāci — when shall such a cry arise in my speech? Yat samanantaram eva sphurati puras tāvakī mūrtiḥ — that your form shines forth immediately before. Gāḍhagāḍhabhavadaṅghrisarojāliṅganavyasanatatparacetāḥ — with mind intent on embracing your lotus-feet ever more deeply. Vastv avastv idam ayatnata eva tvāṃ kadā samavalokayitāsmi — when shall I see you, this thing and non-thing, effortlessly?

Stotra 10 (avicchedabhaṅga): na soḍhavyam avaśyam te jagadekaprabhor idam — this is not to be endured, of you, sole Lord of the world. Māheśvarāś ca lokānām itareṣāṃ samāś ca yat — and the Māheśvaras and the equals of the worlds. Ye sadaivānurāgeṇa bhavatpādānugāminaḥ — those who always follow your feet with love. Yatra tatra gatā bhogāṃs te kāṃś cid upabhuñjate — wherever they go, they enjoy some enjoyments. Bhartā kālāntako yatra bhavāṃs tatra kuto rujaḥ — where you are the Lord, the ender of time, where is pain? Tadaiva sarvaḥ kālo 'sya tvadānandena pūryate — at that moment, all his time is filled with your bliss. Ānandarasabindus te candramā galito bhuvi — your drop of bliss-nectar is the moon fallen to earth. Sūryas tathā te prasṛtaḥ saṃhārī tejasaḥ kaṇaḥ — and the sun is your ray of destroying light. Baliṃ yāmas tṛtīyāya netrāyāsmai tava prabho — we offer to the third eye, to you, Lord. Alaukikasya kasyāpi māhātmyasyaikalakṣmaṇe — to the unique mark of some unearthly greatness. Tenai va dṛṣṭo 'si bhavaddarśanādyo 'tihṛṣyati — by that alone you are seen; he who sees you rejoices exceedingly. Kathañcid yasya vā harṣaḥ ko 'pi tena tvam īkṣitaḥ — by whom, somehow, some joy; by that you are seen. Yeṣām prasanno 'si vibho yair labdhaṃ hṛdayaṃ tava — Lord, to whom you are gracious, by whom your heart is gained. Ākṛṣya tvatpurāttais tu bāhyam ābhyantarīkṛtam — drawing from your city, making the external internal. Tvad ṛte nikhilaṃ viśvaṃ samadṛgyātam īkṣyatām — without you, the whole world is seen as equal (indifferent). Īśvaraḥ punar etasya tvam eko viṣamekṣaṇaḥ — but for this, you alone are the Lord, the odd-eyed one. Āstāṃ bhavatprabhāveṇa vinā sattaiva nāsti yat — let it be: without your power, there is no being at all. Tvaddūṣaṇakathā yeṣām tvad ṛte nopapadyate — whose talk of your faults does not cohere without you. Bāhyāntarāntarāyālīkevale cetasi sthitiḥ — abiding in the mind that is merely external-internal-obstacle. Tvayi cet syān mama vibho kim anyad upayujyate — if it is in you, Lord, what else is useful to me? Anye bhramanti bhagavann ātmany evātiduḥsthitāḥ — others wander, Lord, extremely unsettled in the self. Anye bhramanti bhagavann ātmany evātisusthitāḥ — others wander, Lord, extremely settled in the self. Apītvāpi bhavadbhaktisudhām anavalokya ca — even without seeing the nectar of devotion to you. Tvām īśa tvatsamācāramātrāt siddhyanti jantavaḥ — Lord, beings succeed by mere conduct similar to yours. Bhṛtyā vayaṃ tava vibho tena trijagatāṃ yathā — we are your servants, Lord; as for the three worlds. Bibharṣy ātmānam evaṃ te bharttavyā vayam apy alam — you bear yourself; so we too are to be borne, enough. Parānandāmṛtamaye dṛṣṭo 'pi jagadātmani — seen in the world-self, though filled with supreme bliss-nectar. Tvayi sparśarase 'tyantatarasutkaṇṭhito 'smi te — I am extremely desirous of the taste of touching you. Deva duḥkhāny aśeṣāṇi yāni saṃsāriṇām api — Lord, all the sufferings that belong to saṃsārins. Ghṛtyākhyabhavadīyātmayutāny āyānti sahyatām — named 'ghee,' united with your self, become bearable. Sarvajñe sarvaśaktau ca tvayy eva sati cinmaye — you being omniscient, omnipotent, consciousness itself. Sarvathāpy asato nātha yuktāsya jagataḥ prathā — Lord, in every way, the world's appearance is asato (unreal). Tvatprāṇitāḥ sphurantīme guṇā loṣṭopamā api — these qualities, though like clods, shine, animated by you. Nṛtyanti pavanoddhūtāḥ kārpāsāḥ picavo yathā — as cotton wisps dance, blown by wind. Yadi nātha guṇeṣv ātmābhimāno na bhavet tataḥ — Lord, if there were no self-conceit in the qualities. Kena hīyeta jagatas tvadekātmatayā prathā — by what would the world's appearance as one-self-with-you be diminished? Vandyās te 'pi mahīyāṃsaḥ pralayopagatā api — those too are venerable, the great ones, even those who have attained dissolution. Tvatkopapāvakasparśapūtā ye parameśvara — those purified by the touch of your anger-fire, Lord. Mahāprakāśavapuṣi vispaṣṭe bhavati sthite — when the great light-body stands clearly manifest. Sarvato 'pīśa tat kasmāt tamasi prasarāmy aham — Lord, from all sides, why do I spread into darkness? Avibhāgo bhavān eva svarūpam amṛtaṃ mama — you alone are the undivided, my own form, immortal. Tathāpi martyadharmāṇām aham evaikam āspadam — and yet, for mortal dharmas, I alone am the single support. Maheśvareti yasyāsti nāmakaṃ vāgvibhūṣaṇam — he who has the ornament of speech, the name 'Maheśvara.' Praṇāmāṅkaś ca śirasi sa evaikaḥ prabhāvitaḥ — with the mark of bowing on his head, he alone is made manifest. Sadasac ca bhavān eva yena tenāprayāsataḥ — you are both real and unreal; by that, effortlessly. Svarasenaiva bhagavaṃs tathā siddhiḥ kathaṃ na me — Lord, by its own nature, how is success not mine? Śivadāsaḥ śivaikātmā kiṃ yan nāsādayet sukham — Śiva's servant, one-self with Śiva; what happiness would he not attain? Tarpyo 'smi devamukhyānām api yenāmṛtāsavaiḥ — I am to be satisfied by the immortal nectar of the chief gods. Hṛnnābhyor antarālasthaḥ prāṇināṃ pittavigrahaḥ — the bile-bodied one abiding between heart and navel. Grasase tvaṃ mahāvahniḥ sarvaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam — you, the great fire, consume all, moving and unmoving.

Stotra 11 (autsukyaviśvasita): jagad idam athavā suhṛdo bandhujano vā na bhavati mama kim api — this world, or friends, or relatives — nothing is mine. Tvaṃ punar etat sarvaṃ yadā tadā ko 'paro me 'stu svāmin — but you are all this; when that is so, who else is mine, Lord? Maheśvaras tvaṃ sākṣāt sarvaṃ jagat tvam eveti — you are Maheśvara directly; the whole world is you. Vastv eva siddhim etv iti yācñā tatrāpi yācñaiva — even the prayer 'may it succeed' is itself a prayer. Tribhuvanādhipatitvam apīha yat tṛṇam iva pratibhāti bhavajjuṣaḥ — even lordship of the three worlds appears like straw to one devoted to you. Kim iva tasya phalaṃ śubhakarmaṇo bhavati nātha bhavatsmaraṇād ṛte — what fruit of good karma, Lord, without remembrance of you? Yena naiva bhavato 'sti vibhinnaṃ kiñcanāpi jagatāṃ prabhavaś ca — by which there is nothing separate from you, and you are the source of worlds. Tvadvijṛmbhitam ato 'dbhutakarmasv apy udeti na tava stutibandhaḥ — hence, even in wonderful deeds, your praise-hymn does not arise. Tvannay o 'smi bhavadarcananiṣṭhaḥ sarvadāham iti cāpy avirāmam — I am made of you, ever devoted to seeing you; thus without ceasing. Bhāvayann api vibho svarasena svapnago 'pi na tathā kim iva syām — even envisioning, Lord, by its own nature, even in a dream, how could I be thus? Ye manāg api bhavaccaraṇābjodbhūtasaurabhalavena vimṛṣṭaḥ — those touched even slightly by the fragrance from your lotus-feet. Teṣu visram iva bhavati samastaṃ bhogajātam amarair api mṛgyam — for them, all enjoyments become rest, sought even by immortals. Hṛdi te na tu vidyate 'nyad anyad vacane karmaṇi cānyad eva śaṃbho — in the heart, nothing else; but in speech and action, something else, Śambhu. Paramārthasato 'py anugraho vā yadi vā nigraha eka eva kāryaḥ — whether grace or restraint, one thing is to be done. Mūḍho 'smi duḥkhakalito 'smi jarādidoṣabhīto 'smi śaktirahito 'smi tavāśrito 'smi — I am deluded, afflicted with suffering, afraid of old age and the rest, powerless; I take refuge in you. Śambho tathā kalaya śīghram upaimi yena sarvottamāṃ dhuram — Śambhu, so arrange quickly that I attain the highest burden. Apojjhitaduḥkhamārgaḥ — having abandoned the path of suffering. Tvatkarṇadeśam adhiśayya mahārghabhāvam ākranditāni mama tucchatarāṇi yānti — having placed them at your ear, my trivial cries attain great value. Vaṃśāntarālapatitāni jalaikadeśakhaṇḍāni mauktikamaṇitvam ivodvahanti — like fragments of bamboo falling into water attaining the state of pearl-gems. Kim iva ca labhyate bata na tair api nātha janaiḥ kṣaṇam api kaitavād api ca ye tava nāmni ratāḥ — what is not obtained by those, Lord, who are devoted to your name, even for a moment, even from deceit. Śiśiramayūkhaśekhara tathā kuru yena mama kṣatamaraṇo 'ṇimādikam upaimi yathā vibhavam — O moon-crested one, so arrange that I attain, with broken death, the vibhūti of aṇimā etc. Śambho śarva śaśaṅkaśekhara śiva tryakṣākṣamālādhara — Śambhu, Śarva, moon-crested, Śiva, three-eyed, wearing the rosary. Śrīmann ugrakapālalāñchana lasadbhīmatriśūlāyudha — glorious, marked with the terrible skull, shining with the terrible trident. Kāruṇyāmbunidhe trilokaracanāśīlograśaktyātmaka — ocean of compassion, characterized by the terrible power of creating the three worlds. Śrīkaṇṭhāśu vināśayāśubhabharān ādhat svasiddhiṃ parām — Śrīkaṇṭha, quickly destroy the mass of inauspiciousness; bestow supreme siddhi. Tat kiṃ nātha bhaven na yatra bhagavān nirmātṛtām aśnute — what, Lord, would not happen where the Lord assumes creatorship? Bhāvaḥ syāt kim u tasya cetanavato nāśāsti yaṃ śaṅkaraḥ — what being would have destruction, which Śaṅkara protects? Itthaṃ te parameśvarākṣatamahāśakteḥ sadā saṃśritaḥ — thus, taking refuge always in your imperishable great power. Saṃsāre 'tra nirantarādhividhuraḥ kliśyāmy ahaṃ kevalam — in this saṃsāra, I suffer, afflicted with continuous distress, alone. Yady apy atra varapradoddhatatamāḥ pīḍājarāmṛtyava ete — even though here the most excellent of boons — pain, old age, death — these. Vā kṣaṇam āsatāṃ bahumataḥ śabdādir evāsthiraḥ — or for a moment, the much-desired, speech etc., impermanent. Tatrāpi spṛhayāmi santatasukhākāṅkṣī ciraṃ sthāsnave — even there I desire, longing for constant happiness, to stay long. Bhogāsvādayutatvadaṅghrikamaladhyānāgrya jīvātave — for the sake of living, with meditation on your lotus-feet united with the taste of enjoyment. He nātha praṇatārtināśanapaṭo śreyonidhe dhūrjaṭe — Lord, destroyer of the distress of the bowed, treasure of welfare, matted-haired one. Duḥkhaikāyatanasya janmamaraṇatrastasya me sāmpratam — of me, the abode of suffering alone, afraid of birth and death, now. Tac ceṣṭasva yathā manojñaviṣayāsvādapradā uttamā — so arrange that excellent, mind-pleasing enjoyment-taste be given. Jīvann eva samaśnuve 'ham acalāḥ siddhīs tvadarcāparaḥ — while living, may I attain, O devotee of your worship, the immovable siddhis. Namo mohamahādhvāntadhvaṃsanānanyakarmaṇe — homage to the destroyer of the great darkness of delusion, whose action is unique. Sarvaprakāśātiśayaprakāśāyendulakṣmaṇe — to the one whose light surpasses all light, marked by the moon.

Stotra 12 (rahasyanirdeśa): sahakāri na kiñcid iṣyate bhavato na pratibandhakaṃ dṛṣi — no helper is needed by you, no obstacle for the seer. Bhavataiva hi sarvam āplutaṃ katham adyāpi tathāpi nekṣase — all is flooded by you alone; how is it that you are not seen even now? Api bhāvagaṇād apīndriyapracayād apy avabodhamadhyataḥ — from the host of things, from the collection of senses, from the midst of knowledge. Prabhavantam api svataḥ sadā paripaśyeyam apoḍhaviśvakam — I would always see you, self-born, having removed the universe. Kathaṃ te jāyeran katham api ca te darśanapathaṃ vrajeyuḥ — how would they arise; how would they enter the path of seeing you? Kenāpi prakṛtimahatāṅkena khacitaḥ — adorned with some great prakṛti-mark. Tathotthāyotthāya sthalajalatṛṇāder akhilataḥ — rising up again and again from all earth, water, grass. Padārthadyānsṛṣṭisravadamṛtapūrair(?) vikirasi sākṣatkṛta bhavadrūpaprasṛtāmṛtatarpitāḥ — you scatter the flowing nectar of creation, having directly realized your form; satisfied by the nectar flowing from your form. Unmūlitatṛṣo mattā vicaranti yathāruci — with thirst uprooted, they wander as they wish, intoxicated. Na tadā na sadā na caikadety api sā yatra na kāladhīr bhavet — not then, not always, not even once — where the thought of time is not. Tad idaṃ bhavadīyadarśanaṃ na ca nityaṃ na ca kathyate 'nyathā — this seeing of you is not eternal, nor is it spoken of otherwise. Tvadvilokanasamutkacetaso yogasiddhir iyatī sadāstu me — may the siddhi of yoga be always this much for me, whose mind is eager to see you. Yad viśeyam abhisandhimātratas tvatsudhāsadanam arcanāya te — I would enter, by mere intention, the abode of your nectar, for worship of you. Nirvikalpabhavadīyadarśanapraptiphullamanasāṃ mahātmanām — of great souls whose minds bloom from obtaining the non-conceptual seeing of you. Ullasanti vimalāni helayā ceṣṭitāni ca vacāṃsi ca sphuṭam — pure actions and words clearly shine forth, playfully. Bhavanbhavadīyapādayor nivasann antara eva nirbhayaḥ — dwelling within, in your lotus-feet, fearless. Bhavabhūmiṣu tāsu tāsv ahaṃ prabhum arceyam anargalakriyaḥ — in those and those worlds, I would worship the Lord, with unobstructed action. Bhavadaṅghrisaroruhodare parilīno galitaparaiṣaṇaḥ — absorbed in the interior of your lotus-feet, with desires fallen away. Atimātramadhūpayogataḥ paritṛpto vicareyam icchayā — satisfied by the excessive use of honey, I would wander as I wish. Yasya dambhād iva bhavatpūjāsaṅkalpa utthitaḥ — whose resolve to worship you arose as if from pride. Tasyāpy avaśyam uditaṃ sannidhānaṃ tavocitam — even for him, your fitting presence necessarily arises. Bhagavann itarān apekṣiṇā nitarām ekarasena cetasā — Lord, by one who depends on others, with mind of one taste. Sulabhaṃ sakalopaśāyinaṃ prabhum ātṛpti pibeyam asmi — easily, the Lord who rests in all, I would drink to satisfaction. Kim tvayā nirākṛtam sarvaṃ heyam etat tad eva tu — what is rejected by you, all that is to be abandoned; that alone. Tvannayaṃ samupādeyam ity ayaṃ sārasaṃgrahaḥ — 'your way is to be adopted' — this is the essence. Bhavato 'ntaracāri bhāvajātaṃ prabhuvanmukhyatayaiva pūjitaṃ tat — the host of beings abiding in you is worshipped as chief, by your being Lord. Bhavato bahir apy abhāvamātrā katham īśān bhavet samarcyate vā — outside you, mere non-being — how, Lord, could it be or be worshipped? Niḥśabdaṃ nirvikalpaṃ ca nirvyākṣepam athānisam — silent, non-conceptual, without distraction, always. Kṣobhe 'py adhyakṣamī kṣeyaṃ tryakṣa tvām eva sarvataḥ — even in agitation, the object to be known, O three-eyed one, is you alone everywhere. Prakaṭaya nijadhāma deva yasmiṃs tvam asi sadā parameśvarīsametaḥ — reveal your own abode, Lord, where you are always with the Supreme Lady. Prabhucaraṇarajaḥsamānakakṣyāḥ kim aviśvāsapadaṃ bhānti bhṛtyāḥ — do servants not appear trustworthy, equal to the dust of the master's feet? Darśanapatham upayāto 'py apasarasi kuto mameśa bhṛtyasya — even having entered the path of seeing, why do you withdraw, Lord, from your servant? Kṣaṇamātrakam iha na bhavasi kasya na jantor dṛśor viṣayaḥ — for a moment here you are not; whose eye's object are you not? Aikyasaṃvidamṛtācchadhārayā santataprasṛtayā kadā vibho — when, Lord, by the constantly flowing cover of the nectar of non-dual awareness? Plāvanāt paramabhedamānayaṃs tvāṃ nijaṃ ca vapur āpnuyāṃ mudam — from the flood, bringing supreme non-difference, may I attain you and my own body with joy. Aham ity amuto 'varuddhalokād bhavadīyāt pratipattisārato me — 'I' — from the closed-off world, from the essence of your recognition, for me. Aṇumātrakam eva viśvaniṣṭhaṃ ghaṭatāṃ yena bhaveyam arcitā te — may even an atom of the world's stability happen, by which I may be your worshipper. Aparimitarūpam ahaṃ taṃ taṃ bhāvaṃ pratikṣaṇaṃ paśyan — seeing each thing, unlimited in form, moment by moment. Tvām eva viśvarūpaṃ nijanāthaṃ sādhu paśyeyam — may I rightly see you alone, world-formed, my own Lord. Bhavadaṅgagataṃ tam eva kasmān na manaḥ paryaṭatīṣṭam artham artham — why does my mind not wander toward that, your limb-dwelling, desired object? Prakṛtikṣatir asti no tathāsya mama cecchā paripūryate — the damage to nature is not so; if my desire is fulfilled. Paraiva śataśaḥ kila te tavānubhāvād bhagavan ke 'py amunaiva cakṣuṣā ye — a hundredfold superior, Lord, by your power, some with this very eye. Api hālikaceṣṭayā carantaḥ paripaśyanti bhavadvapuḥ sadāgre — even those moving with a ploughman's effort see your form always before. Na sā matir udeti yā na bhavati tvadicchāmayī sadā śubham — that mind does not arise which is not always made of your will, auspicious. Athetarad bhagavataivam ācaryate — and otherwise, Lord, it is so arranged. Ato 'smi bhavadātmako bhuvi yathā tathā sañcaran sthito 'niśam — therefore I am your-self on earth, moving and standing always as it is. Abādhitatvadamalaṅghripūjotsavaḥ — with the festival of worship of your stainless lotus-feet, unobstructed. Bhavadīyagabhīrabhāṣiteṣu pratibhā samyag udetu me puro 'taḥ — may my understanding arise rightly before me in your deep words. Tadanuṣṭhitaśaktir apy atas tadbhavadarcāvyasanaṃ ca nirvirāmam — and then, having exercised that power, the devotion to your worship, without cessation. Vyavahārapade 'pi sarvadā pratibhātv arthakalāpa eṣa mām — in the sphere of transaction too, always, may this collection of meanings shine for me. Bhavato 'vayavo yathā na tu svata evādaraṇīyatāṃ gataḥ — as your part, not having attained lovability by itself. Manasi svarasena yatra tatra pracaraty apy aham asya gocareṣu — in the mind, by its own nature, wherever it wanders, I am in its domains. Prasṛto 'py avilola eva yuṣmatparicaryācaturaḥ sadā bhaveyam — even when gone forth, may I always be undisturbed, skilled in your service. Bhagavan bhavadicchayaiva dāsas tava jāto 'smi parasya nātra śaktiḥ — Lord, by your will alone I have become your servant; no other has power here. Katham eṣa tathāpi vaktrabimbaṃ tava paśyāmi na jātu citram etat — how is it that I never see your face; this is not strange. Samutsukās tvāṃ prati ye bhavantaṃ pratyartharūpād avalokayanti — those eager for you who see you as an opposing form. Teṣām aho kiṃ tadupasthitaṃ syāt kiṃ sādhanaṃ vā phalitaṃ bhavet tat — for them, ah, what would be present; what means or fruit would arise? Bhāvā bhāvatayā santu bhavadbhāvena me bhava — let things be as things; be for me with your bhāva. Tathā na kiñcid apy astu na kiñcid bhavato 'nyathā — let there be nothing, and nothing otherwise from you. Yan na kiñcid api tanna kiñcid apy astu kiñcid api kiñcid eva me — what is not anything, let that not be anything; let there be something, just something, for me. Sarvathā bhavatu tāvatā bhavān sarvato bhavati labdhapūjitaḥ — in every way, let it be; by that much, you are everywhere, having received worship.
sivst-p03.inference: Stotras 9–12 shift from svātantrya (autonomy/freedom) in devotional mode to the arcane lore (rahasya). The devotee's stance: 'I am yours, make me free.' The key experience is āveśa (possession by the deity) — the devotee is so filled with Śiva that the distinction between worshipper and worshipped dissolves. The devotional voice cajoles, longs, and surrenders. This is the 'soul of the practices' (Gitananda): the feeling and emotional intensity with which the upāyas are done. The key move: the devotee's wisdom is an obstacle (tvadantarvasatir mūko bhaveyaṃ — dwelling within you, may I be silent; otherwise I am wise); silence (āveśa) is the goal. And the arcane lore (rahasya): 'your way is to be adopted' — this is the essence.
sivst-p03.conclusion: Autonomy in devotional mode: the devotee surrenders autonomy to Śiva. Āveśa (possession by the deity) dissolves the worshipper/worshipped distinction. The devotional voice cajoles, longs, surrenders. The arcane lore (rahasya): 'your way is to be adopted' — this is the essence. Key: tvadantarvasatir mūko bhaveyaṃ (dwelling within you, may I be silent) and tvannayaṃ samupādeyam (your way is to be adopted).

sivst-p04.question: What is the self (ātman) in devotional mode?
premises: Stotra 13 (saṃgraha): saṃgrahena sukhaduḥkhalakṣaṇaṃ māṃ prati sthitam idaṃ śṛṇu prabho — hear, Lord, what is established for me regarding happiness and suffering. Saukhyam eṣa bhavatā samāgamaḥ svāminā viraha eva duḥkhitā — happiness is union with you; suffering is separation from you. Antaram api atitarām aṇīyasī yā tvadaprathanakālikāsti me — even internally, the tiniest thing that is your non-manifestation. Tām apīśa parimṛjya sarvataḥ svaṃ svarūpam amalaṃ prakāśaya — remove it entirely, Lord, and reveal your own pure self. Tāvake vapuṣi viśvanirbhare citsudhārasamaye niratyaye — in your body, full of the world, the flow of consciousness-nectar, imperishable. Tiṣṭhataḥ satatam arcataḥ prabhuṃ jīvitaṃ mṛtam athānyad astu me — may my life and death and all else be for worshipping you, Lord. Īśvaro 'ham aham eva rūpavān paṇḍito 'smi subhago 'smi ko 'paraḥ — I am the Lord; I am the form; I am the learned one; I am the fortunate one; who else? Matsamo 'sti jagatīti śobhate mānitā tvadanurāgiṇaḥ param — the world is like me — the pride of the devoted one is glorious. Devadeva bhavadadvayāmṛtākhyātisaṃharaṇalabdhajanmanā — Lord of gods, you are the gatherer of non-dual bliss. Tad yathāsthitapadārthasaṃvidā māṃ kuruṣva caraṇārcanocitam — by the knowledge of established things, make me fit for worshipping your feet. Dhyāyate tad anu dṛśyate tataḥ spṛśyate ca parameśvaraḥ svayam — meditation, then seeing, then touching — the Lord reveals himself. Yatra pūjanamahotsavaḥ sa me sarvadāstu bhavato 'nubhāvataḥ — where the festival of worship is, may it always be for me by your power. Yady athāsthitapadārthadarśanaṃ yuṣmadarcanamahotsavaś ca yaḥ — if seeing established things and the festival of worshipping you are paired. Yugmam etad itaretarāśrayaṃ bhaktiśāliṣu sadā vijṛmbhate — that pair is mutually dependent and arises in the devoted. Tattadindriyamukhena santataṃ yuṣmadarcanarasāyanāsavam — continuously, by every sense, the nectar of worshipping you is drunk. Sarvabhāvacaṣakeṣu pūriteṣv āpibann api bhaveyam unmadaḥ — all bhāvas filled with cups, intoxicated, I would be. Anyavedyam aṇumātram asti na svaprakāśam akhilaṃ vijṛmbhate — no other knowable, even an atom; all shines by self-light. Yatra nātha bhavataḥ pure sthitaṃ tatra me kuru sadā tavārcituḥ — where, Lord, your temple is established, there may I always be the worshipper. Dāsadhāmni viniyojito 'py ahaṃ svecchayaiva parameśvara tvayā — even placed in the abode of servants, I, by my own will, am devoted to you, Lord. Darśanena na kim asmi pātritaḥ pādasaṃvahanakarmaṇāpi vā — by seeing, what am I not made fit for? By the act of worshipping your feet, even? Śaktipātasamaye vicāraṇaṃ prāptam īśa na karoṣi karhicit — śaktipāta at the time of consideration is attained, Lord; you never delay. Adya māṃ prati kim āgataṃ yataḥ svaprakāśanavidhau vilambase — what has come to me today? Why do you delay in revealing yourself? Tatra tatra viṣaye bahirvibhāty antare ca parameśvarīyutam — there and there, the thing shines external and internal, united with the Goddess. Tvāṃ jagattritayanirbharaṃ sadā lokayeya nijapāṇipūjitam — may I always see you, full of the three worlds, worshipped by my own hands. Svāmisaudham abhisandhimātrato nirvibandham adhiruhya sarvadā — the Lord's abode, by mere intention, without obstacle, always ascending. Syāṃ prasāda paramāmṛtāsavāpānakeliparilabdhanirvṛtiḥ — may I be the joy obtained by drinking the nectar of grace. Yatsamastasubhagārthavastuṣu sparśamātravidhinā camatkṛtim — by the mere touch, wonder at all beautiful things. Tāṃ samarpayati tena te vapuḥ pūjayanty acalabhaktiśālinaḥ — they offer that; by that, the acalabhakti-possessors worship your form. Sphārayasy akhilaṃ ātmanā sphuran viśvam āmṛśasi rūpam āmṛśan — you expand all, shining, touching the form, touching the world. Yat svayaṃ nijarasena ghurṇase tat samullasati bhāvamaṇḍalam — what you yourself stir with your own nectar, that world-circle shines forth. Yo 'vikalpam idam arthamaṇḍalaṃ paśyatīśa nikhilaṃ bhavadvapuḥ — who sees this world-circle without concept, Lord, entirely your form. Svātmapakṣaparipūrite jagaty asya nityasukhinaḥ kuto bhayam — in the world filled with one's own side, for the eternally happy one, where is fear? Kaṇṭhakoṇaviniviṣṭam īśa te kālakūṭam api me mahāmṛtam — Lord, even the poison at the throat is, for me, great nectar. Apy upāttam amṛtaṃ bhavadvapur bhedavṛtti yadi rocate na me — even if taken, the nectar of your form, if difference-activity pleases, not for me. Tvatpralāpamayaraktagītikāni tyayuktavadanopaśobhitaḥ — adorned with the hymn of your speech, red with devotion. Syām athāpi bhavadarcanakriyāpreyasīparigatāśayaḥ sadā — may I be, always, with mind pervaded by the beloved act of seeing you. Īhitaṃ na bata pārameśvaraṃ śakyate gaṇayituṃ tathā ca me — the desire for the supreme Lord cannot be counted, so for me. Dattam apy amṛtanirbharaṃ vapuḥ svaṃ na pātum anumanyate — even given, the self, full of nectar, does not consent to drink. Tathā tvām agādham avikalpam advayaṃ svaṃ svarūpam akhilārthaghasmaram — so you, deep, non-conceptual, non-dual, self-form, devourer of all objects. Āviśann aham umeśa sarvadā pūjayeyam abhisaṃstuvīya ca — entering, O Lord of Umā, may I always worship and praise.

Stotra 14 (jayastotra): jayalakṣmīnidhānasya nijasya svāminaḥ puraḥ — homage to the treasure of victory-lakṣmī, my own Lord. Jayodghoṣaṇapīyūṣarasam āsvādaye kṣaṇam — may I taste the nectar of the victory-proclamation for a moment. Jayai karudraikaśiva mahādeva maheśvara — victory to the one-eyed, Śiva, Mahādeva, Maheśvara. Pārvatīpraṇayiñ śarva sarvagīrvāṇapūrvaja — Pārvatī's beloved, Śarva, first of all gods. Jaya trailokyanāthaikalāñchanālikalocana — victory to the lord of the three worlds, with one eye, the crescent. Jaya pītartalokārtikālakūṭāṅkakandhara — victory to the bearer of the yellow, the arka, the poison at the throat. Jaya mūrtatriśaktyātmiśataśūlollasatkara — victory to the three-śakti-bodied, with the hundred-trident shining hand. Jayecchāmātrasiddārthapūjārhacaraṇāmbuja — victory to the one whose lotus-feet are worshipped by mere will. Jaya śobhaśatasyandilokottaravapurdhara — victory to the bearer of a body surpassing the world, with a hundred glories. Jayaikajaṭikākṣīṇagaṅgākṛtyāttabhasmaka — victory to the one with one matted lock, who drank the Gaṅgā, wearing ashes. Jaya kṣīrodaparyastajyotsnācchāyānulepana — victory to the one anointed with the moonlight of the milk-ocean. Jayeśvarāṅgasaṅgottharatnakāntāhimaṇḍana — victory to the one adorned with gems arising from the contact of the Lord's body. Jayākṣayaikaśītāṃśukalāsadṛśasaṃśraya — victory to the one whose refuge is like the imperishable, single, cool crescent. Jaya gaṅgāsadārbdhaviśvaiśvaryābhiṣecana — victory to the one anointed with the Gaṅgā, the lordship of the world. Jayādharāṅgasaṃsparśapāvanīkṛtagokula — victory to the one who purified Gokula by the touch of the lower body. Jaya bhaktimadābaddhagoṣṭhīniyatasannidhe — victory to the one constantly present in the assembly bound by devotion. Jaya svecchātapodeśavipralambhitabāliśa — victory to the one who, by the region of self-willed heat, has distanced the foolish. Jaya gaurīpariṣvaṅgayogyasaubhāgyabhājana — victory to the vessel of good fortune fit for Gaurī's embrace. Jaya bhaktirasārdrārdrabhāvopāyanalampaṭa — victory to the one greedy for the offering of bhāva soaked in bhakti-nectar. Jaya bhaktimadoddāmabhaktavāṅnṛttatoṣita — victory to the one pleased by the dance of the devotees' speech. Jaya brahmādideveśaprabhāvaprabhavavyaya — victory to the one who is the source and expenditure of the power of Brahmā and the gods. Jayalokeśvaraśreṇiśirovidhṛtaśāsana — victory to the one whose command is held on the heads of the world-lords. Jayasarvajagannyastasvamudrāvyaktavaibhava — victory to the one whose glory is manifest by his own seal placed on all the world. Jayātmadānaparyantaviśveśvaramaheśvara — victory to Maheśvara, the lord of the world, up to the giving of the self. Jaya trailokyasargecchāvasarāsaddvitīyaka — victory to the one without a second, the occasion of the will for the creation of the three worlds. Jayaiśvaryabharodvāhadevīmātrasahāyaka — victory to the one whose sole helper is the goddess, the bearer of the weight of lordship. Jayākramasamākrāntasamastabhuvanatraya — victory to the one who has pervaded all three worlds by sequence. Jayāvigītam ābālagīyamāneśvaradhvane — victory to the Lord's sound, sung by children, unblemished. Jayānukampādiguṇānapekṣasahajonnate — victory to the one naturally elevated, without regard for qualities like compassion. Jaya bhīṣmamahāmṛtyughaṭanāpūrvabhairava — victory to Bhairava, the unprecedented one who arrays the great death of the terrible. Jaya viśvakṣayoccaṇḍakriyāniṣparipanthika — victory to the one unobstructed in the fierce action of world-destruction. Jaya śreyaḥśataguṇānuganāmānukīrtana — victory to the one whose name is chanted by hundreds of good ones. Jaya helāvitīrnaitadamṛtākarasāgara — victory to the one who has effortlessly crossed this ocean of nectar. Jaya viśvakṣayakṣepikṣaṇakopāśuśukṣaṇe — victory to the one who quickly, in a moment, throws the world into destruction. Jaya mohāndhakārāndhajīvalokaikadīpaka — victory to the single lamp of the world of beings blinded by the darkness of delusion. Jaya prasuptajagatījāgarūkādhipūruṣa — victory to the Lord of the waking world, asleep. Jaya dehādrikuñjāntarnikūjañjīvajīvaka — victory to the living one chirping within the cave of the body-mountain. Jaya sanmānasavyomavilāsivarasārasa — victory to the one playing in the sky of the good mind, the essence of rasa. Jaya jāmbūnadodagradhātūdbhavagirīśvara — victory to the Lord of the mountain arising from the excellent Jāmbūnada gold. Jaya pāpiṣu nindolkāpātanotpātacandramaḥ — victory to the moon that casts the thunderbolt of censure on the sinful. Jaya kaṣṭatapaḥkliṣṭamunidevadurāsada — victory to the one hard to approach for the gods and munis distressed by harsh austerity. Jaya sarvadaśārūḍhabhaktimallokalokita — victory to the one seen by the world of bhaktas risen in all states. Jaya svasampatprasarapatrīkṛtanijāśrita — victory to the one who has made his own dependents the spread of his own wealth. Jaya prapannajanatālālanaikaprayojana — victory to the one whose sole purpose is the cherishing of the surrendered people. Jaya sargasthitidhvaṃsakāraṇaikāvadānaka — victory to the one who is the sole cause of creation, maintenance, and destruction. Jaya bhaktimadālolalīlotpalamagotsava — victory to the one who is the festival of the lotus-play of the intoxicated bhaktas. Jaya jayabhājana jaya jitajanmajarāmaraṇa — victory to the vessel of victory, victory to the conqueror of birth, old age, and death. Jaya jagajjyeṣṭha jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya tryakṣa — victory to the eldest of the world; victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, O three-eyed one.

Stotra 15 (bhaktistotra): the knots of the three malas are for those who have crossed; yogis, scholars, the healthy — they are truly devoted to you. Those nourished by māyīya, kalā, rāga etc. move happily on the world's shore, devoted to you. Devotees, distinct in praise and worship, are not dispassionate nor Śiva nor desiring liberation — they worship you. May I be intoxicated with the wine of high devotion, worshipping you from within the heart. The devotees, from within and without, offer to you, Lord, the nectar of devotion. Dharma and adharma, knowledge and action, happiness and suffering — devotees taste something of all, ah. Even the blind and leprous shine, ornamented with the supreme devotion to you. Even those who worship you from outside, with mind alone, Lord — protect, increase, honor this great wealth of devotion. Lord, your community of devotees, though attached to you, may it always be pleased. The devotion, growing, becomes the eternal one of Śambhu, absorbed in my mind. Even if the milk-jar is obtained, the greed for curds is killed — what is this incomplete attainment, what is the chief happiness? Devotion, always eternal, growing, becomes absorbed in the mind. Even external and internal, the supreme fragrances of Śaṅkara's garland, the devotees are permeated. Even the yogi, residing near, is permeated by the fragrance — all beings are permeated. Light exists; say nothing more; the whole universe, though in deep sleep, is entirely. Where, Lord, the worshipper of Śiva is established, there may the crest-jewels of Śaṅkara's feet-shining remain. May the darkness of delusion be destroyed, for the destruction of the tri-guṇa and the world-path. Even if happiness was never enjoyed for long, thus I am born useless; Śaśidhara's feet have trodden my supreme head. May the devotees of Śiva quickly have long, long great wealth.

Stotra 16 (pāśānudbheda): nothing at all is an obstacle for the beings regarding your covering; nothing at all is an obstacle for the devotees regarding your covering. Even with means, with distinctions, the devotees' self, once purified, shines. Victory to those intoxicated with the nectar of devotion to you; who can be compared to them? May the nectar of devotion to you be ever-increasing for me; let me be intoxicated with devotion, angry, shouting 'Śiva!' Even fierce, varied, may I be devoted to you, Lord. For devotees, there is nothing to be known; you are non-conceptual, established in yourself. Devotees, pierced by sharp goosebumps, even suffering becomes enjoyment. Even those whose consciousness is entirely drenched with your moonlight, wherever they are, inside or outside. For devotees, even the external covering of you is equally sweet; some, bewildered, see the form as separate. For devotees, the mind is stainless, free from honor and dishonor, passion and aversion. How could one like the world be among devotees? The darkness of passion and aversion is conquered by the light of devotion. Among the great, who are the knowers? He whose devotion to you is the means of siddhi. The fame of the devoted is sought; he by whom you alone are worshipped. Liberation is named for the ripened devotion to you, Lord. In that, the first state is attained; we are like the liberated; even the arrival of suffering is great for me. May your separation not be, Lord; even the stream of happiness. You are pleased by devotion; when you are pleased, Lord, what? That mutual dependence is fitting, as you alone know. Whether with form or without, within or without, for the devoted self, Lord, you are entirely nectar. In this world, for the devoted to you, the fruit of happiness is established elsewhere. Secretly, devotion; beyond, devotion; devotion is the name of the supreme in you, Lord. Devotion, devotion, devotion — the name is exceedingly intense. May my devotion be intense, supreme, in you. Because of that, all the glory of beings is born from you; whatever is, or is not, let it be something, just something, for me. In every way, let it be; by that much, you are everywhere, having received worship.
sivst-p04.inference: Stotras 13–16 turn to the self (ātman) in devotional mode. The devotee's stance: 'I am Śiva's; the self is not separate from Śiva.' The key experience is ātmaikya (oneness of self) — the devotee recognizes that the self is Śiva, not a separate soul. Stotra 13 (saṃgraha): summary — happiness is union with you, suffering is separation; remove the non-manifestation, reveal your pure self. Stotra 14 (jayastotra): glorification — victory to Śiva, the supreme, the one without a second. Stotra 15 (bhaktistotra): about devotion — devotees are not dispassionate nor Śiva nor desiring liberation; they worship you; may I be intoxicated with the wine of high devotion. Stotra 16 (pāśānudbheda): breaking fetters — nothing is an obstacle for devotees; the mind is stainless; even suffering becomes enjoyment; liberation is named for ripened devotion.
sivst-p04.conclusion: Self in devotional mode: the devotee recognizes the self as Śiva, not as a separate soul. Ātmaikya (oneness of self) — the devotee's self is Śiva's self. The stotras move from summary (saṃgraha) to glorification (jayastotra) to devotion (bhaktistotra) to breaking fetters (pāśānudbheda). Key: stotra 13's īśvaro 'ham aham eva rūpavān (I am the Lord; I am the form) and stotra 16's bhaktir upacīyamānā yeyaṃ śambhoḥ sadātanī (devotion, growing, becomes the eternal one of Śambhu).
sivst-p04.theorem: ātmaikya (oneness of self) in devotional mode: the devotee's self is Śiva's self; bhakti ripens into liberation.

premises: Stotra 17 (divyakrīḍā): aho ko 'pi jayaty eṣa svāduḥ pūjāmahotsavaḥ — ah, what a sweet festival of worship, ah, what a delightful play! Vyāpārāḥ siddhidāḥ sarve ye tvatpūjāpuraḥsarāḥ — all activities that are for the worship of devotees are siddhis. For devotees, all your forms are themselves siddhis; they worship you without ceasing. The time of worship is always the time of worship for devotees; there is no beginning or end. Even in dream, even in delusion, the festival of your worship is established for devotees. Not only for those who chant, offer, bathe, meditate — for devotees, the festival of your worship is always. For devotees, the festival of worship is superior to that of Indra and Brahmā. What is to be obtained is obtained only by devotees; they know it. Standing in your consciousness-form, with the actions of the 36 tattvas, I worship you always, Lord. With body, speech, mind, and effort, I worship you, Lord; devotees enjoying the festival of worship. Let all time pass, even the infinite; I beg only this, Lord: the festival of the nectar of worship. The festival of worship grows daily; may it bear fruit for me. In the ocean of you, the great self, worshipping, may I always dwell. Even the mind, offered to devotees, is sweet in the festival of worship. For devotees, sending the nectar of worship, the activities of the senses. For devotees, intoxicated with the heat of devotion, what other cause of nirvāṇa is there than immersion in the nectar of worship? May the festival of the nectar of worship be the cause of your grace for me, Lord. May I experience, Lord, moment by moment, the great joy of drinking the nectar of worship. For devotees, the endeavor of worship is itself the accomplished; what is unattainable is attained by them. For devotees, the festival of worship is the supreme; even the gods are inferior. For devotees, the festival of worship is the wealth; even the great are inferior.

Stotra 18 (āviṣkāra): jagato 'ntarato bhavantam āptvā punar etad bhavato 'ntarāl labhante — having obtained you, the Lord of the world, within, they obtain the world again from within you. Lord of the world, your devotion is not far for them; there is nothing distant for them. The world is your self; there is no difference between the world and you for devotees. (Repeated throughout — the refrain of non-difference.)

Stotra 19 (udyotana): prārthanābhūmikātītavicitraphaladāyakaḥ — the prayer-transcending, fruit-giving, wonderful tree of Śiva — the supreme goal. The self is not you, Lord; you alone are the supreme. May my mind, absorbed in your consciousness-nectar, be freed from the cave of Māyā. May I see your pure face, Lord, by the nectar of knowledge. May your form, dripping with immortal nectar, fill me. May all my desires, even the paired ones, be offered to you, Lord. May the pure rays of you come to me. May the thieves of qualities, who steal the supreme truth, be subdued. May my mind be filled with the nectar of devotion to you, Lord. May all the latent tendencies be washed away, having plunged into the state of liberation. May I, desiring siddhi, not be stopped by pride, Lord. May the servant's liberation be granted by the Lord quickly. May the lotus-feet of you, the treasure of immortal nectar, always bloom in my mind. May I, a devotee, be in the world, not different from you. May the supreme goal be attained; may I be your devotee, not other. May I, even in the waking state or another, be devoted to you; may I be your devotee, not other.

sivst-p05.inference: Stotras 17–20 close the Śivastotrāvalī. The devotional arc completes: bhakti as supreme (p01) → recognition in devotional mode (p01) → svātantrya (p02) → autonomy (p03) → self (p04) → closing (p05). The closing stotras bring bhakti and jīvanmukti together: bhakti is the supreme path, and the devotee is liberated in this life. The text's final word: bhakti is not different from recognition; they are one. The key move in p05 is the identification of bhakti with recognition: bhakti is not different from pratyabhijñā; they are one. The refrain of non-difference (the world is your self) runs through stotra 18 and 20, identifying bhakti with the recognition that all is Śiva.
sivst-p05.conclusion: The Śivastotrāvalī closes with bhakti and jīvanmukti together. Bhakti is the supreme path; the devotee is liberated in this life. The text's final word: bhakti is not different from recognition (pratyabhijñā); they are one. The refrain of non-difference (the world is your self) identifies bhakti with the recognition that all is Śiva. Key: stotra 17's bhaktānāṃ tvanmayāḥ sarve svayaṃ siddhaya eva te (for devotees, all your forms are themselves siddhis) and stotra 20's the world is your self (repeated).
sivst-p05.theorem: bhakti = pratyabhijñā (not different); bhakti is the supreme path; jīvanmukti through bhakti. The world is Śiva's self; there is no difference.
